title: Deutsche Bank joins Notabene's trust network as it brings digital asset custody to institutional customers
summary: Deutsche Bank has joined the Notabene network, adding a trusted layer for digital asset transactions to the bank’s own risk management processes for its custody service.
body_markdown:
**NEW YORK, Nov 16, 2026 —**


Notabene, which operates the trust network for regulated digital asset transactions, announced that Deutsche Bank has joined the Notabene network, adding a trusted layer for digital asset transactions to the bank’s own risk management processes for its custody service. Deutsche Bank will use Notabene to exchange originator and beneficiary information with other digital-asset service providers before transfers settle, as required under the EU Transfer of Funds Regulation and FATF Travel Rule requirements.


Deutsche Bank announced its digital asset custody solution on September 16, 2026, for institutional and corporate clients in Europe, including corporates, asset managers, hedge funds, custodians, brokers and sovereign institutions. At launch, Deutsche Bank will support a selected range of digital assets, including Bitcoin and Ether, as well as selected stable coins or e-money tokens, including USDC and EURC, EURAU. The range of supported assets may be expanded over time, subject to client demand and the bank’s product-approval, risk management and regulatory processes. Tokenized financial instruments are also included in the roadmap.


In traditional payments, information about who is sending and who is receiving a transaction is carried by existing traditional payment systems. Public blockchains have no native equivalent, so each regulated institution has to identify its counterparty and exchange the required data itself, for every transfer. Notabene gives Deutsche Bank one connection to thousands of crypto-asset service providers across a multitude of global jurisdictions, with data end-to-end encrypted and exchanged directly between institutions in line with applicable data protection requirements. This is what allows institutions to benefit from the speed, cost, and programmability of digital assets without sacrificing the trust and security that they demand.


> "Bringing digital assets to our clients means holding them to the standards already expected from us. Connecting to Notabene's network lets us deliver on the level of trust demanded by customers, by exchanging the required counterparty information securely with other institutions before settlement." **Paul Maley, Global Head of Trust & Securities Services at Deutsche Bank.**


Notabene is built to the standards banks already operate under. The platform is SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified, data is end-to-end encrypted, and counterparty information follows IVMS101, the global Travel Rule data standard. Notabene's network also supports ISO 20022, the messaging standard used across bank payment systems, so digital asset transactions can connect to the payment infrastructure institutions already run.


> "Banks have relied on a shared messaging layer for half a century to know who is on the other side of a payment. Public blockchains don't come with one, our network is that trust layer for digital assets." **Alice Nawfal, CEO and co-founder of Notabene.**


‍


**About Notabene**


Founded in 2020 and headquartered in New York, Notabene operates the largest open network of on-chain transactions, enabling 300+ institutions — such as Deutsche Bank, Ripple, Copper, Crypto.com, OKX, and more — to confirm and verify counterparties in real time, authorize transactions before settlement, and unlock compliant B2B stablecoin payments. Notabene connects thousands of trusted counterparties, facilitating trillions of dollars in transaction volume annually across over 115 jurisdictions. To learn more, visit[notabene.id](http://notabene.id/) .


**About Deutsche Bank**


Deutsche Bank provides retail and private banking, corporate and transaction banking, lending, asset and wealth management products and services as well as focused investment banking to private individuals, small and medium-sized companies, corporations, governments and institutional investors. Deutsche Bank is the leading bank in Germany with strong European roots and a global network.
